evidence.claim: High mountains and barren plateaus connect fossil quarries and museums
evidence.quote: Some of the world's most significant dinosaur fossil quarries and museums are clustered along this route

evidence.claim: The Dinosaur Diamond loops through western Colorado and eastern Utah, crossing high mountains and barren plateaus between fossil quarries and museums.
evidence.quote: Length: 134 miles (486 miles total CO/UT)

evidence.claim: crossing high mountains and barren plateaus between fossil quarries and museums.
evidence.quote: The byway traverses high mountains and barren plateaus

evidence.claim: Colorado DOT highlights the dinosaur collections and the Colorado and Green rivers along this National Scenic Byway, designated in 2002.
evidence.quote: Dinosaur Diamond was designated by the U.S. Secretary of Transportation as a National Scenic Byway in 2002.

evidence.claim: the Colorado and Green rivers
evidence.quote: two great rivers of the West(the Colorado and Green)

evidence.claim: It lists 486 miles for the two-state loop and suggests two to three days.
evidence.quote: Length: 134 miles (486 miles total CO/UT) Driving time: two to three days

evidence.claim: On the Colorado leg, Highway 139 crosses 8,205-foot Douglas Pass, with a few switchbacks and a seven-percent grade on its south side.
evidence.quote: Douglas Pass, elevation 8,205 feet (2,501 meters), is a mountain pass in the Book Cliffs of western Colorado.

evidence.claim: Highway 139 crosses
evidence.quote: is traversed by State Highway 139.

evidence.claim: a few switchbacks and a seven-percent grade on its south side.
evidence.quote: the road, though reasonably steep on the south side (7%), has no tight spots and only a few switchbacks.

evidence.claim: The loop joined roads with separate histories.
evidence.quote: The following Colorado routes are included in the Colorado portion of the Dinosaur Diamond Scenic and Historic Byway:

evidence.claim: Near Moab, residents campaigned for a riverbank road to replace the difficult Heavenly Stairway pack trail.
evidence.quote: Moab residents pushed for a road to be built along the riverbank.

evidence.claim: the difficult Heavenly Stairway pack trail.
evidence.quote: Access between Moab and Castle Valley was originally via a pack trail called the Heavenly Stairway. This trail, named for a dramatic descent of over 1,000 feet (300 m), was described as beautiful, but difficult to navigate.

evidence.claim: King's Toll Road replaced that trail by 1902, improving travel but remaining vulnerable to flooding because it lay too low beside the river.
evidence.quote: By 1902, the trail was replaced with a toll road, called King's Toll Road, after Samuel King.

evidence.claim: improving travel but remaining vulnerable to flooding because it lay too low beside the river.
evidence.quote: While the road did improve travel, it was not built high enough above the river level and was often flooded.

evidence.claim: Colorado designated its byway in 1997 and Utah its Prehistoric Highway in 1998, before national recognition joined them in 2002.
evidence.quote: The segment within Colorado was designated the Dinosaur Diamond Scenic and Historic Byway by the Colorado Transportation Commission in 1997. The segment within Utah was designated the Dinosaur Diamond Prehistoric Highway by the Utah State Legislature in 1998. The highway was approved as a National Scenic Byway in 2002.

evidence.claim: Starting west of Fruita, follow I-70 toward Cisco and SR 128 toward Moab, then turn north through Green River, Price and Helper.
evidence.quote: State Route 128, from the Cisco Road running to US-191 near Moab; US Route 191, from SR-128 running to I-70 at Crescent Junction; Interstate 70, from US-191 at Crescent Junction running to US-6 near Green River; US Route 6, from I-70 running to US-191 near Helper;

evidence.claim: Starting west of Fruita, follow I-70 toward Cisco
evidence.quote: I-70 between Grand Junction and the Utah state line.

evidence.claim: US 191 climbs toward Duchesne; US 40 continues east through Vernal and Jensen toward Dinosaur.
evidence.quote: Within Duchesne, US 40 and US 191 diverge, and the DD continues 55 miles (89 km) south along US 191 over an unnamed mountain pass

evidence.claim: US 40 continues east through Vernal and Jensen toward Dinosaur.
evidence.quote: It lies along the Green River and U.S. Route 40, southeast of the city of Vernal

evidence.claim: US 40 continues east through Vernal and Jensen toward Dinosaur.
evidence.quote: Upon leaving Dinosaur, the DD continues west on US 40 and crosses the border into Utah.

evidence.claim: The quarry is a separate excursion north of Jensen.
evidence.quote: the Dinosaur Quarry is located in Utah, north of the town of Jensen, Utah.

evidence.claim: Return through Rangely and over Douglas Pass to Fruita and the interstate.
evidence.quote: Just west of Fruita, the byway turns north onto SH-139, traveling 78 miles (126 km) to the next town of Rangely, and traversing the Douglas Pass.

evidence.claim: Return through Rangely
evidence.quote: The byway continues 18 miles (29 km) northwest on SH-64, to the small town of Dinosaur.

evidence.claim: Two sheer sandstone walls frame the Price River near the mouth of Price Canyon, giving Castle Gate its name.
evidence.quote: its name was derived from a rock formation near the mouth of Price Canyon. This formation features two sheer sandstone walls on either side of the Price River

evidence.claim: The mining town developed after the railroad crossed the Wasatch Plateau; its first mine opened around 1886 and supplied coal for steam trains.
evidence.quote: The first coal mine, named the Castle Gate Mine #1, opened around 1886, after the Denver and Rio Grande Western Railroad constructed its Utah Division over the Wasatch Plateau, from the town of Springville. The mine produced high-quality coal for the steam trains.

evidence.claim: When Castle Gate incorporated in 1914, the Utah Fuel Company and the Denver and Rio Grande Western Railroad owned and tightly controlled the town.
evidence.quote: In 1914, Castle Gate was incorporated as a town, which was owned and tightly controlled by the Utah Fuel Company and the D&RGW

evidence.claim: An explosion at Mine No. 2 killed 172 miners in 1924.
evidence.quote: On March 8, 1924, the Utah Fuel Company's Castle Gate Mine #2 exploded, killing 172 miners.

evidence.claim: The town itself was dismantled in 1974, and residents moved to a subdivision west of Helper.
evidence.quote: Castle Gate was dismantled in the summer of 1974, and residents were relocated to a new subdivision at the mouth of Spring Canyon, west of Helper.

evidence.claim: Coal-loading facilities replaced the former townsite beside the railway.
evidence.quote: The former townsite was cleared and replaced with coal-loading facilities neighboring the railroad line.

evidence.claim: The Wall of Bones holds thousands of fossils in a rock layer tilted 67 degrees from horizontal.
evidence.quote: The "Wall of Bones" located within the Dinosaur Quarry building in the park consists of a steeply tilted (67° from horizontal) rock layer which contains thousands of dinosaur fossils.

evidence.claim: Earl Douglass found eight Apatosaurus vertebrae here in 1909 while working for the Carnegie Museum.
evidence.quote: Paleontologist Earl Douglass of the Carnegie Museum discovered eight vertebrae of an Apatosaurus on August 17, 1909

evidence.claim: Rivers had carried the animals into the sediments that became solid rock; mountain building later lifted and tilted those layers, and erosion exposed them.
evidence.quote: The dinosaurs and other ancient animals were carried by the river system which eventually entombed their remains in Utah.

evidence.claim: mountain building later lifted and tilted those layers, and erosion exposed them.
evidence.quote: The pile of sediments were later buried and lithified into solid rock. The layers of rock were later uplifted and tilted to their present angle by the mountain building forces that formed the Uinta Mountains during the Laramide orogeny. Erosion later exposed the layers at the surface to be found by paleontologists.

evidence.claim: The quarry building needed its own engineering response to the ground: after structural problems forced closure in 2006, the Park Service rebuilt the exhibit hall on steel columns reaching bedrock.
evidence.quote: The Park Service successfully rebuilt the Quarry Exhibit Hall, supporting its weight on 70-foot steel micropile columns that extend to the bedrock below the unstable clay.

evidence.claim: structural problems forced closure in 2006
evidence.quote: In July 2006, the Quarry Visitor Center was closed due to structural problems

evidence.claim: The quarry reopened in 2011.
evidence.quote: The Dinosaur Quarry was reopened in Fall 2011.

evidence.claim: The town sits in the high desert of the Colorado Plateau, with the Colorado River and Book Cliffs among its surrounding features.
evidence.quote: Fruita is located in the high desert climate zone on the Colorado Plateau. Surrounding the city limits is the Colorado River, the Colorado National Monument and the Book Cliffs range

evidence.claim: Dinosaur Hill earned its name through the bones found there, including a Brontosaurus skeleton discovered by Elmer Riggs and his crew in 1901.
evidence.quote: In 1901, Riggs and crew found nearly two thirds of a Brontosaurus skeleton on the northeast side of Dinosaur Hill, in Fruita.

evidence.claim: Riggs worked with a Field Museum crew from Chicago.
evidence.quote: paleontologist Elmer Riggs and crew, from the Field Museum of Natural History in Chicago

evidence.claim: They recovered nearly two-thirds of that skeleton, and other sauropod bones followed.
evidence.quote: Later, other sauropod bones were also found, which eventually led to the landmark's name.

evidence.claim: The animals came from the late Jurassic and lay within the Morrison Formation.
evidence.quote: The animals were from the late Jurassic Age (150 million years ago) and within the 600-foot-thick (180 m) Morrison Formation.

evidence.claim: Colorado DOT includes the Dinosaur Journey Museum in Fruita among the byway features.
evidence.quote: Dinosaur Journey Museum 550 Jurassic Court Fruita CO 81521
